sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily the first time it is accessed.
sketches.resonance: Loneliness isn't an error or an edge case; the language guarantees there will only ever be one.

sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining with `?.` — if any link in the chain is nil, the entire expression silently evaluates to nil without crashing.
sketches.resonance: Each attempt to reach deeper into memory returns nothing; the silence of nil propagates without complaint, the way grief quietly empties every room it touches.

sketches.mechanism: Prolog's closed-world assumption: anything not provable from the knowledge base is considered false. An empty database answers every query with failure.
sketches.resonance: In a world where nothing has been said about you, every question about whether you mattered fails — not because it's untrue, but because no one recorded the proof.
